subject: Clarify surge supplement and discount structure for short evaluation
messages:

Cc: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 7 Sep 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Quick question on extension + burst pricing for our 30d eval

Hi Karthik / Marissa,

Thanks again for the walkthrough last week — really helpful. We need to firm up how Redwood bills if we exceed the time-boxed allowance during the 30-day evaluation. Two quick asks from procurement and engineering: 

- If we hit a surge (spike in inference volume) during the eval, do we pay per-token overage or is there a one-time surge supplement?
- Can you provide an example pricing tie-out if we go 40% over our expected tokens in week 2?

Attached is the eval request doc and a short usage snapshot from August to help calibrate. Procurement is trying to decide between asking for a short extension vs. accepting a capped surge supplement.

Can someone send a short options table (cost delta + impact on conversion credits) we can show leadership?

Appreciate it —
Samantha
ClearGrid — Director, AI Integrations
Attachments: ClearGrid_Eval_Request_v1.pdf (application/pdf), usage_snapshot_aug.csv (text/csv)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha@cleargrid.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 8 Sep 2026 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick question on extension + burst pricing for our 30d eval

Samantha — thanks for the note and the attachments. Quick response and I'll follow up with a short spreadsheet by EOD explaining the numbers. High level options from our side: 

1) Surge supplement (pay-as-you-go with a capped multiplier)
   - Overages billed at standard per-token rate up to 20% over baseline, then a surge supplement multiplier (1.6x) for the remaining overage during the eval window.
   - Pros: no contract amendment; keeps procurement paperwork light.
   - Cons: higher marginal cost during sustained surges.

2) Short extension (add 14 days to the eval, same locked rate + small extension fee)
   - Extension fee = 10% of the forecasted eval consumption (covers reserved slot planning).
   - Pros: predictable unit economics, easier to credit against conversion if you convert to paid plan.
   - Cons: requires a signed addendum (simple 1-page).

3) Hybrid: small extension (7 days) + reduced surge multiplier (1.25x) for bursts beyond that window

Example tie-out based on your usage_snapshot_aug.csv (rounded):
- Baseline estimate for 30d: 1.2M tokens at $0.0009/token = $1,080
- If week 2 spikes +40% across overall eval (1.68M tokens):
   Option 1 (surge): first 20% overage billed at $0.0009, remaining 28.8% billed at $0.00144 (1.6x) => total ~$1,512
   Option 2 (14d extension): locked rate => prorated charge + 10% extension fee => total ~$1,260

I'll put these numbers into a one-pager. Two quick Qs for clarity:
- If procurement prefers credits instead of invoice-level fees, do they want those credits redeemable on conversion?
- Any internal SLA concern (e.g., run beyond eval that needs fallback model routing)?

Looping in Marissa for formal discount/credit guidance and David for the SRE implications.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer | Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks Karthik — this is helpful. Procurement prefers credits redeemable on conversion; leadership wants the path with the lowest upside billing risk (they'd rather flip to a paid plan than eat a surprise invoice). A couple clarifications: 

- Can the extension fee be fully credited back if we sign a paid contract within 30 days?
- For the surge multiplier, can you provide a softened cap (e.g., capped at +35% cost vs baseline) rather than a pure multiplier?

Michael is on this thread for procurement-level approval. We're hoping for a tight answer so we can include it in the vendor comparison doc.

Samantha

Samantha — appreciate the nuance here. From a commercial perspective we can do the following to reduce leader-level risk and keep procurement paperwork minimal: 

- Extension fee creditability: 100% credit against your first paid invoice if you convert within 30 days of the addendum signature.
- Surge cap option: instead of a multiplier above 20%, we can offer a soft cap at +35% cost vs baseline. That means your maximum bill for the eval would be limited to ~1.35x the baseline estimate in the example Karthik sent.
- Credits: We can issue eval credits instead of discounts; credits are redeemable on conversion and expire 90 days after conversion (standard).

If that sounds acceptable I'll get Legal to prepare a 1-page addendum (no complex procurement). Marissa — would you like me to include standard SLA fallback language or keep it simple?

—Marissa Cole
